title: introduce-cost-tuner-conductor-and-quant-sampler-daemon
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We need a low-friction way to generate conservative, tenant-aware batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles from production-like traffic without impacting live latency SLOs. Previous autotuners ran as heavy, centralized jobs and produced profiles that were brittle across tenant traffic shapes. This PR introduces two components: (1) Cost Tuner Conductor – an orchestration service to coordinate short, prioritized sampling campaigns (campaigns run across a rolling set of serving nodes, collect lightweight telemetry, and produce compact profile candidates), and (2) Quant Sampler Daemon – a tiny, non-blocking process co-located with the serving runtime that samples activation statistics and cache-hit patterns at P95/P99-safe sampling rates.

review_comments: Ravi Singh - Can the sampler be throttled dynamically when node CPU > 70%? (concern for noisy neighbors)
Ava Martinez - Reply: yes; sampler reads node telemetry and uses an exponential backoff policy. Configurable via cost_tuner.throttle.cpu_threshold.
Marta Lopez - Suggestion: make the campaign results include a stability score and sample-count so tenants can opt into conservative vs aggressive profiles.
Ava Martinez - Reply: added stability_score to campaign result proto and surfaced in the API response. See services/cost-tuner/campaign/state.go commit.
Dmitri Kozlov - Tests: please add an e2e that runs a short campaign against a synthetic traffic replay (so we can detect regressions in sampling overhead).
Ava Martinez - Reply: added tests/integration/cost_tuner_smoke_test.go which runs with local replay harness; CI runs this with mocked telemetry.

release_notes: Add Cost Tuner Conductor service and Quant Sampler Daemon. Enables safe, low-overhead campaigns to derive tenant-aware batching/caching defaults and quantization profile candidates. Guided rollout: start in staging for 48h, then canary to 5% traffic. See docs/ops/cost_tuning.md for instructions and safety knobs.
testing_and_telemetry: Local + CI: unit tests and a synthetic replay integration test. On staging we ran 3 sample campaigns across two tenant archetypes (chatbot-heavy, short-completion API) collecting ~24k sample vectors each. Telemetry exported: sampled activation histograms, batch-shape counters, per-tenant KV-cache hit traces (low-res). Overhead observed: <0.9% CPU on sampled nodes at default throttle, no measurable change in P95 latency beyond noise.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy conductor + daemon in staging, run 3 campaigns (24h) per tenant archetype. 2) Validate stability_score and sample-count thresholds in UI. 3) Canary in prod at 5% traffic for 2 days with automated rollback if p95 latency or error rate increases beyond guardrails. 4) Gradually enable suggested profiles for opt-in tenants, and expose conservative default to all after two weeks of negative-regression-free telemetry.
migration_notes: No schema migrations that affect existing runtime configs. New config: cost_tuner.* (default safe values included). Backwards compatible: sampler disabled by default; operator must enable daemonset through helm values. Profiles produced are advisory until explicitly applied.
security_considerations: Sampler only collects aggregated histograms and counters; no raw payload or PII leaves nodes. Data is encrypted in transit via existing mTLS channels. We audited proto messages to ensure no request payloads are serialized.
notes_for_reviewers: Key areas to focus review on: campaign state machine correctness (idempotency), backpressure/throttling logic in daemon, and telemetry export efficiency. I intentionally kept sampling windows short (1-5s) to avoid KV-cache pollution.
